items.note: およぎます → およぐ: the ぎ before ます becomes ぐ. Compare およぐのもすきです.

items.note: かきます here, かく in えをかくのがすきですか. Same verb, two forms: ます to state the action, dictionary form to feed のが.

items.note: The pastime, so it works after すき (suki): サイクリングがすきです (saikuringu ga suki desu). じてんしゃにのる (jitensha ni noru) is the act of riding.
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: a hobby noun for this lesson's すき (suki) frame.

items.note: Contrast チャンさんはワインがすきです, which likes the WINE. This one likes the drinking of it.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2b (constructed for systematic coverage; job: forms — のむ was carded bare only; also a minimal pair against the base lesson's ワインがすきです).
items.target: チャンさんはワインをのむのがすきです

items.note: Regular 1: はしります → はしる. Compare はしるのがじょうずです, which needs the dictionary form.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2b (constructed for systematic coverage; job: forms — はしります appeared in no sentence).
items.target: ラジャさんはよくはしります

items.note: A noun plus する (suru), the dictionary form of します (shimasu). The polite form is かんこうします (kankō shimasu).
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: a noun-plus-する (suru) verb in the dictionary form this lesson introduces.

items.note: The lesson's core frame: person は — thing が — すきです. にほんの here means "of Japan", i.e. Japanese.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (from the book: Target Dialogue, Paul's line; job: the lesson's headline sentence, uncarded).
items.target: わたしはにほんのアニメがすきです

items.note: The pair to たなかさんはにほんごをはなします: を stays with はなす, and の wraps the whole action so が can mark it as the thing liked.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2b (constructed for systematic coverage; job: forms — はなす was carded bare only, and this completes the ます/dictionary pair).
items.target: にほんごをはなすのがすきです

items.note: みるの turns the verb into the thing liked — the nominalizer only ever follows a dictionary form. Contrast にほんのアニメ, where の joins two nouns instead.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: particles — minimal pair against わたしはにほんのアニメがすきです, the possessive の).
items.target: アニメをみるのがすきです

items.english: Paul-san and Suzuki-san like mecha anime.
items.note: と joins the two people into one topic, so は marks them both and the sentence takes a single すきです.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (from the book: Target Dialogue closing summary; job: と joining subjects inside the person は thing が frame).
items.target: ポールさんとすずきさんはロボットのアニメがすきです

items.scene: after agreeing you like the same anime the other person does
items.note: かくの is "drawing" — the nominalizer の turns the dictionary form into something が/も can mark. も (not が) because it is one MORE thing you like.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (from the book: Target Dialogue, Suzuki's line; job: のも, the nominalizer under a second particle).

items.note: Same frame, negated: です becomes じゃありません. A な-adjective never takes くない.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: forms — fixed frame for the な-adjective grid, present negative).
items.target: ポールさんはやきゅうがすきじゃありません

items.english: What kind of sports do you like?
items.note: どんな + noun + がすきですか narrows a category you have already established the person likes.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (from the book: EXERCISES III example and SPEAKING PRACTICE 1; job: the どんな question on スポーツ, carded only for アニメ and くだもの).
items.target: どんなスポーツがすきですか

items.english: Do you like drawing pictures, Green-san?
items.note: え is what かく takes as its object (を), and the whole action えをかく is what の turns into the thing liked (が). Two different particles, two different jobs.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (from the book: EXERCISES VII substitution 2; job: を inside a のが clause, the pattern's hardest shape).
items.target: グリーンさんはえをかくのがすきですか

items.note: This の joins two nouns: いとこ の ポール, "Paul, [who is] my cousin." It is the same の as にほんのアニメ, and NOT the nominalizer の of かくのがすきです — that one only ever follows a verb.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (from the book: Target Dialogue; job: possessive/appositive の, and the contrast with this lesson's nominalizer の).

items.scene: answering "what kind of Italian food do you like?"
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (from the book: EXERCISES III substitution 2 answer; job: the only sentence ピザ appears in).

items.note: のる (noru) takes に (ni), not を (o): じてんしゃにのる (jitensha ni noru), never じてんしゃをのる (jitensha o noru).
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: a dictionary-form verb on Lesson 7's じてんしゃ (jitensha), and the に (ni) it takes is the part a learner gets wrong.

items.scene: answering "what kind of anime do you like?"
items.note: ロボットのアニメ is literally "robot anime" — の narrows the noun that follows it.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (from the book: Target Dialogue, Paul's answer; job: the answer half of どんな〜がすきですか).
items.target: ロボットのアニメがすきです

items.note: Built the same way as this lesson's イタリアりょうり (itaria ryōri): a country in front of りょうり (ryōri).
items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: a second example of the country plus りょうり (ryōri) pattern, so it reads as a slot rather than a fixed phrase.

items.note: No object, so のが attaches straight to the dictionary form. あるきます → あるく is the other form EXERCISES V asks for.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2b (constructed for systematic coverage; job: forms — あるく was carded bare only, and this is the のが pattern at its simplest).

items.english: What kind of music do you like?

items.target: どんなおんがくがすきですか

items.note: うた is the noun "song", so it takes が directly. うたうのがじょうずです — with the verb — says the same thing about the ACT of singing.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: vocabulary — the only sentence うた appears in, plus the noun/verb contrast).

items.note: すいえい (suiei) is a NOUN meaning swimming as a sport or discipline, so it needs します to become something you do: まいしゅう すいえいを します (maishū suiei o shimasu), 'I swim every week'. しゅみは すいえい です (shumi wa suiei desu) = 'my hobby is swimming'. For the physical act, use およぐ (oyogu).
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-3) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: Lesson 15 teaches suiei and the sport/hobby set

items.english: Do you like going to art museums, Emma-san?
items.note: に stays with いく inside the clause; の then wraps the whole action so が can mark it.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: particles — に surviving inside a のが clause, in question form).
items.target: エマさんはびじゅつかんにいくのがすきですか

items.note: The ます-form as the sentence's own verb. Its dictionary form うたう is what のが needs: うたうのがすきです, "likes singing".
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2b (constructed for systematic coverage; job: forms — うたいます appeared in no sentence, only as a bare vocabulary card, while its dictionary form was already used in one).
items.target: ポールさんはよくうたいます

items.note: Regular 1: あるきます → あるく. The き before ます becomes く.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 1 (from the book: EXERCISES V item 9, which asks for this form; job: a dictionary form the exercise names and no card carried).

items.note: が, not も: this is what you like, full stop. うたうのもすきです would mean singing is one MORE thing you like on top of something already mentioned.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: particles — minimal pair against the base lesson's うたうのもすきです).

items.note: します → する is Irregular, the third class in the chart along with きます → くる.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: forms — のが on an Irregular verb, completing the chart's three classes).
items.target: たなかさんはスポーツをするのがすきです

items.note: The longest form in the set, and still only the ending changes: じょうず + じゃありません + でした.

items.target: すずきさんはダンスがじょうずじゃありませんでした

items.note: りょうり on its own is "cooking" or "cuisine"; にほんの narrows it, the same way イタリアりょうり does.
items.reviewNote: Extras wave 2 (constructed for systematic coverage; job: vocabulary — the only sentence the bare りょうり appears in).

items.note: じょうず is only ever said about OTHER people. Japanese speakers avoid it about themselves or their own family because it sounds like boasting — which is also why じょうずですか is rarely asked.

items.note: Contrast with サッカーをみるのがすきです: this one likes the SPORT, that one likes WATCHING it. A plain noun takes が on its own; an action needs のが to become one.

items.note: Dictionary form of あいます (aimasu, "meet", Lesson 9). Regular 1: the い before ます becomes う.
items.reviewNote: Verb dictionary-form batch (2026-09). あいます was carded in Lesson 9 with no dictionary form anywhere in the deck; the book never prints this one.

items.note: Dictionary form of あげます (agemasu, "give", Lesson 14). Regular 2, so ます simply becomes る. Lesson 15's grammar names あげます in its own list of the Regular 2 verbs taught up to that point, precisely so this form can be derived.
items.reviewNote: Verb dictionary-form batch (2026-09). Recovery, not an invention: Lesson 15 GRAMMAR 2 enumerates あげます among the Regular 2 verbs introduced through Lesson 14, and the dictionary form was never carded.

items.note: Dictionary form of あります (arimasu, Lesson 12), and it covers every sense this deck teaches that verb in: "be, exist", "have", and "there is, takes place". Regular 1: the り before ます becomes る. Its animate partner います (imasu, "be, exist") has the dictionary form いる (iru).
items.reviewNote: Verb dictionary-form batch (2026-09). あります is carded three times across Lessons 12, 14 and 16 with three senses; one dictionary-form card serves all three, so the note names them rather than splitting the card.

items.note: Dictionary form of おくります (okurimasu, "send", Lesson 9). Regular 1: the り before ます becomes る, the same change as のります → のる.
items.reviewNote: Verb dictionary-form batch (2026-09). おくります was carded in Lesson 9 with no dictionary form anywhere in the deck.

items.note: Dictionary form of かります (karimasu, "borrow", Lesson 14). It looks like a Regular 1 verb, since り sits before ます, but it is Regular 2: ます becomes る and the り stays, giving かりる and never かる. Lesson 15's grammar lists it among the Regular 2 verbs taught so far for exactly this reason. Contrast かします (kashimasu, "lend"), which really is Regular 1 and gives かす (kasu).
items.reviewNote: Verb dictionary-form batch (2026-09). Recovery: Lesson 15 GRAMMAR 2 enumerates かります among the Regular 2 verbs introduced through Lesson 14, and the dictionary form was never carded. The R1-lookalike trap is the whole reason the book names it.

items.note: Dictionary form of くれます (kuremasu, "give (to me)", Lesson 14). Regular 2: ます becomes る. Pairs with あげる (ageru, "give") the same way くれます pairs with あげます — くれる is used when the thing comes toward you.
items.reviewNote: Verb dictionary-form batch (2026-09). くれます was carded in Lesson 14 with no dictionary form anywhere in the deck.

items.note: Dictionary form of にあいます (niaimasu, "suit, look good on", Lesson 14). Regular 1: the い before ます becomes う, the same change as あいます → あう (au, "meet").
